item.title: Trump Hails Iran Talks, Tehran Sets 'Firm Positions'
item.description: US President Donald Trump said his officials had “very good” talks with Iranian envoys in New York, reviving hopes for a diplomatic off-ramp. Iran meanwhile laid down “firm positions” for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including the US immediately lifting a naval blockade, unfreezing Iranian assets and ending the war “on all fronts”. Speaking to Bloomberg TV, Lizzy Galbraith, senior political economist at Aberdeen said that the fact that talks are happening is better than no talks, but stressed that the key issue is whether either side has actually changed its negotiating position. She noted that the U.S., including Trump and Steve Witkoff, has sounded upbeat, while Iran has framed the meeting as a chance to restate its own demands. Lizzy Galbraith spoke to Stephen Carroll on Bloomberg Daybreak Europe, live from Edinburgh. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Falls as Trump Claims ‘Very Good’ Iran Talks After Annihilation Threat
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
President Donald Trump said US officials had “very good” talks with Iranian envoys in New York, reviving fragile hopes for a new diplomatic off-ramp hours after he again threatened to annihilate the country.
And Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, after a meeting with US President Donald Trump in New York, said he was ready for an energy truce with Russia as a first step toward ending the war, provided Moscow stopped its own attacks on Ukraine’s infrastructure.
Today's guests: Charlotte de Montpellier, ING, Senior Economist, France and Switzerland; Lizzy Galbraith, Aberdeen, Senior Political Economist. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Ready for Truce If Russia Stops Energy Strikes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, after a meeting with US President Donald Trump in New York, said he was ready for an energy truce with Russia as a first step toward ending the war, provided Moscow stopped its own attacks on Ukraine’s infrastructure. Trump has been pushing both sides to halt strikes on energy facilities. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Touts Significant Progress Tackling Asian Scam Syndicates
item.description: A senior Chinese security official said joint law enforcement operations across Southeast Asia have successfully curbed the region’s multibillion dollar cybercrime crisis.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Trump Hails Good US-Iran Talks After Annihilation Threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump said officials held "very good" talks with Iranian envoys in New York. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner participated on behalf of the US. Trump said the three-hour session was "very productive" and another was being planned for the near future. The comments revive hopes for a new diplomatic off-ramp hours after the US president again threatened to annihilate the Islamic Republic. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Tells Judge Trump White House Media Ban Is Lawful
item.description: The US Justice Department urged a federal judge to reject a request by CNN, MS Now and Politico for a court order reinstating White House press credentials for their journalists, after President Donald Trump banned them for what he deemed negative coverage of his administration.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Morocco Football Chief Makes World Cup Final Promise in Election Campaign
item.description: The North African country has spent big on hosting the next World Cup. But an election this week is exposing a deep malaise.
item.dc:creator: Souhail Karam

item.title: Supreme Court Asked to Again Block Missouri’s GOP Voting Map
item.description: The fate of Missouri’s voting maps for the midterm election rests with the US Supreme Court, now that an anti-gerrymandering group has asked justices to yet again prevent state leaders from using a new map that favors Republicans.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: US, Korea Hail ‘Significant Progress’ on $350 Billion Trade Deal
item.description: Donald Trump and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung hailed “significant progress” on implementing the two countries’ long-stalled investment deal, with lawmakers in Seoul saying the first project would be a $22.3 billion gas-fired power development in Texas.
item.dc:creator: Soobin Kim

item.title: Risks Rise for Sara Duterte as Senate Excludes Allies’ Votes
item.description: Sara Duterte, the impeached vice president of the Philippines, is facing an increasing risk of conviction and a lifetime ban on politics after the Senate lowered the vote threshold for a guilty verdict.
item.dc:creator: Andreo Calonzo and Cliff Venzon

item.title: Machado Fails to Slip Into Venezuela While Rodríguez Is Away
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado tried three times in the past 24 hours to return home but was unable to complete the journey.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago and Eric Martin

item.title: Trump, South Korea Want to Get Kim Jong Un Back to Negotiations
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and US President Donald Trump agreed to work closely to help restart dialogue with North Korea, with Trump again expressing his willingness to engage with Kim Jong Un.
item.dc:creator: Heesu Lee

item.title: Japan PM Takaichi Urges UN Security Council Reform
item.description: In her maiden speech to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called for urgent structural reforms to the Security Council. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Grip on GOP Slips as Midterm Election Anxiety Sets In
item.description: As Donald Trump took an aggressive stance on the global stage at the United Nations on Tuesday, several Senate Republicans were breaking from the president back in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis and Erik Wasson

item.title: Burnham Warns UN That AI Can Enhance Russian Disinformation
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday evening accused Russia of spreading lies and disinformation in what he said was an “attack” on society as he revealed plans for a new disinformation center at the heart of his government.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Xi Unlikely to Bring CEOs to Summit Where Trump Seeks Deals
item.description: The highly anticipated summit between President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping will bring together a robust gathering of US corporate leaders, but there will not be a comparable delegation of Chinese executives, raising questions about the prospects for the world’s two largest economies to strike new business deals this week.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron, Kate O'Keeffe, Michelle Jamrisko and Nectar Gan

item.title: British Columbia Leader Eby Calls Snap Election to Cement Power Amid US Tariffs
item.description: British Columbia Premier David Eby called an early election in a bid to consolidate control over the west coast province, capitalizing on his opponents’ disarray and arguing for a fresh mandate amid Canada’s worsening trade war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Seal

item.title: Takaichi Urges UN to Cut Japan’s 1940s-Era ‘Enemy State’ Tag
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged the United Nations to remove references to Japan and Germany as “enemy states,” a classification China has recently seized on to criticize Tokyo after a breakdown in ties over Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale

item.title: Trump Hails Iran Talks Even as Tehran Sets ‘Firm Positions’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said his officials had “very good” talks with Iranian envoys in New York, reviving hopes for a diplomatic off-ramp hours after he threatened to “annihilate” the country’s ruling regime.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Patrick Sykes

item.title: Indonesia Land Reform Law Raises Risk for Plantation, Property
item.description: Indonesia’s passage of a new land reform law could increase risks for plantation companies and property developers by paving the way for new restrictions on corporate landholdings, according to analysts.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono
